description: The last Kiro CLI build that shipped a macOS app, downloaded from the vendor's own URL, so com.amazon.codewhisperer is proved by a real install now that the `kiro-cli` cask installs a bare binary.
why: The bundle id is Kiro CLI's only witness on this machine, so must_find fails if the value is wrong, and must_contain pins the id itself. forbid_rows asserts the cask is absent: its token also names kiro-cli, and with it installed must_find would pass on a wrong bundle id. `kiro` is forbidden because Kiro the IDE is a different product whose ids do not rhyme with this one's, and a change to either entry should rerun this scenario.
known_gaps: The bundle id only. The app is installed and never launched, so the LaunchAgent the cask's old uninstall stanza named, com.amazon.codewhisperer.launcher, is unverified and not in the catalog.
